implementation_notes: The default realization: assert(expr) at the guard points, with the diagnostic the standard requires (expression text, file, line, function) and abort() on failure. The macro is removed by NDEBUG, so it is the right home for internal preconditions and postconditions that should never fire in production.
pitfalls: NDEBUG is normally defined by the release build, so every check disappears; a rule that must hold in production needs an explicit if plus error return or abort.
assert is a function-like macro: commas in the argument that are not parenthesised are read as argument separators.
The predicate must not have side effects (assert(i++ < n)), because the expression is not even compiled under NDEBUG.
abort() is not recoverable: never assert on conditions that user input can violate.

variants.name: C11 static assertion for compile-time invariants
variants.implementation_notes: Invariants over constants - struct sizes, offsets, enum layouts - are checked by the compiler with _Static_assert; the branch disappears entirely from the binary and cannot be disabled at run time. Use it for representation guarantees the rest of the model depends on, and keep assert() for state that only exists at run time.
variants.code_sketch:
_Static_assert(sizeof(struct money) == 16, "money must stay 16 bytes");
_Static_assert(MAX_ORDER_LINES >= 1, "an order always has at least one line");
pitfalls: The expression must be an integer constant expression: sizeof and enum constants qualify, values computed at run time do not.
A failed static assertion stops the build, so anything that legitimately differs between configurations or targets needs #if guards.
